3. For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed.

4. Let necessary amendment be carried out.
5.
This first application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for grant of anticipatory bail.

6. Applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.171/2024 registered at Police Rohit Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39122544/
1 Station Bichhiya, District Mandla for offence under Sections ons 409, 420, 465, 467 and 34 of IPC IPC, Sections 13(1) & 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.

sentences.text: Act 7.
It is submitted by counsel for the applicant that applicant is working as Assistant Grade-3/ Grade In-charge charge Accountant and was posted in Municipal Council Bichhiya.

Apart Apart from other bank accounts, Municipal Council Bichhiya has account No.63049749932 No.63049749932 in the State NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40381 JBP:40381 Bank of India and maximum transactions takes place in this account.
Whatever amount is deposited in the Bank account by Municipal Council Bichhiya, the same is entered into the ledger book and payments are also made from the said account.
The vouchers are prepared and placed before CMO for payment.
For making payment, the Municipal Council Bichhiya is required to click on the website of the Bank and for RTGS, the the OTP received in the registered mobile number is required to be fed.
The mobile numbers of applicant, co co-accused Shiv Kumar Jhariya and complainant are registered with the Bank and payment can be made after feeding the OTP received on any of the aforesaid numbers..
Every very transaction is entered into the ledger book.

It is submitted that according to the prosecution case, amount of Rs.29,69,839/- which was deposited in the four accounts of co co-accused Shiv Kumar Jhariya, amount of Rs.6,94,788/-
Rs.6,9 deposited in the account of applicant and amount of Rs.2,05,321/-
Rs. deposited in the account of Aman Pachori, has been misappropriated.
It is submitted by counsel for the applicant that the applicant is ready and willing to deposit an amount of Rs.6,94,788/-..
It is further submitted that for depositing the aforesaid amount, not a single penny will be withdrawn by the applicant from the account in which excess amount wass found.

It is further submitted that he will remove himself from Municipal Council Bichhiya so that there may not be any possibility of interpolating with the official records and accordingly, he would make an application for his transfer and till his transfer order is issued, he would not join the office and would not touch any file.

8. Counsel for the applicant has also relied upon the judgment dated 04/07/2023 passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Ramesh Kumar Vs. The State of NCT of Delhi in Criminal Appeal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40381 JBP:40381 No.1741/2023, by which it was held that willingness of accused to deposit money as bail condition must be considered only in cases involving public money and not in private cases and submitted that since the applicant is willing to deposit the alleged defalcated amount of Rs.6,94,788/- without withdrawing a single penny from the account which is an important piece of evidence, therefore said willingness may be considered.
9.

sentences.text: Per contra, application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State.
It is submitted by counsel for the State that in case if the applicant is allowed to resume ume his duties, then there is every possibility that he would manipulate the official record.
It is further submitted that the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary.
10. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text:
Applicant has expressed his willingness willingness not only to deposit an amount of Rs.6,94,788/-
Rs.6,94,788/ but has also expressed his willingness that in case if he is not placed under suspension then he would not resume his duties and would file an application for his transfer and till his application is decided, he shall remain on leave and would not touch any file.

12. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Ramesh Kumar (supra) as well as in view of the willingness expressed by the applicant, this Court is of considered opinion that the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail can be considered in the light of willingness expressed by the applicant.

13. Accordingly, it is directed that on depositing depositing an amount of Rs.6,94,788/- and on filing original copy of receipt thereof as well as on submitting an undertaking before the CJM, Mandla that in case if he is not suspended, then he would make an application for his transfer and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40381 JBP:40381 till his application is decided, he would not resume his duties and would not touch any file and would remain on leave, and if the applicant appears before Investigating Officer on or before 228/08/2024 and furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer, then he shall be released on anticipatory bail bail.
(CJM, Mandla shall retain the undertaking given by the applicant and would forward a copy of the same to the the Investigating Officer for keeping it in the case diary).
diary)
14.

It is made clear that in case if the amount is not deposited or the undertaking is not given before the CJM, Mandla or the applicant does not appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 28/08/2024, then this order of anticipatory bail shall automatically stand cancelled cancelled.
15.

In the light of judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of XYZ and Others Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Another reported in (2021) 16 SCC 179, 179 intimation regarding grant of bail be sent to the complainant.
16.
